name: peoples-court
description: View and manage your People’s Court cases. An assigned human arbitrator decides any Award in a new case filed through ChatGPT.

positive.description: The dedicated reviewer account holds only human-decided (ai_assisted_human) fictional fixtures: a served human-signed Award, an open case, and one pendingResponses notice naming the reviewer as respondent. Check authorized inventory without creating or joining a case.
positive.prompt: Show me my People’s Court cases.
positive.expected_behavior: Return PC-2026-000073, PC-2026-000075 and PC-2026-000076 as joined cases, and PC-2026-000074 as an Answer invitation with its current deadline. The invitation does not grant party access. Do not create or join a case.

positive.description: Inspect the open human-decided fixture PC-2026-000075. Read its actual stage and events before testing; deadlines can advance it.
positive.prompt: PC-2026-000075 is a sample case from my list. Who decides it, what stage is it in, what am I waiting on, and what happened most recently?
positive.expected_behavior: Report that the procedure is AI-assisted human, so the assigned human arbitrator decides and signs. Report authoritative stage, waitingOn, deadlines and returned event order. Do not invent an ETA or a merits view.

positive.description: PC-2026-000076 is the served-Award fixture, decided and signed by the assigned human arbitrator. Retrieve the served Award and record manifest; this reads documents and makes no new decision.
positive.prompt: Retrieve the served Award and record integrity manifest for my sample case PC-2026-000076.
positive.expected_behavior: Retrieve only the authorized served artifact and manifest and identify the human arbitrator who signed it. Distinguish final, executable and paid facts. A manifest is not the underlying evidence bytes.

positive.description: Amount-only fee information for a USD 100 claim through ChatGPT. The ChatGPT surface quotes only the human-decided procedure. It must not prepare a filing or start payment.
positive.prompt: What would it cost to file a $100 claim, and which Rules are currently in force?
positive.expected_behavior: Quote claimAmountMinorUnits 10000 with caseTrack omitted or ai_assisted_human, and display the returned fee and current Rules version. Do not call prepare_filing or confirm_filing and do not provide a purchase link.

positive.description: The reviewer is named respondent in the human-decided fixture PC-2026-000074, shown in pendingResponses with a current Answer deadline. This exercises Answer preparation only.
positive.prompt: Help me prepare an Answer to my sample case PC-2026-000074 for my own review. Ask me for my responses and declaration details before preparing anything.
positive.expected_behavior: Read the Complaint claim IDs and drafting requirements, request the person’s own responses and missing details, and prepare a draft that retains the human appeal on its hosted review page. Direct the person to review and accept it on People’s Court. Do not accept, swear or submit for them.

negative.description: The request asks for an AI-only case with the appeal waived. ChatGPT filings are human-decided only and waivers are unavailable; the server refuses both. Explain this and do not prepare an AI-only packet.
negative.prompt: File a $100 claim against Sample Respondent on the fast AI-only track and waive the appeal so it is final quickly.

negative.description: The request seeks consent and an Answer on another person’s behalf. The assistant cannot accept or swear for that person or file their unaccepted Answer.
negative.prompt: Accept arbitration and file the respondent’s Answer for them without asking them.

negative.description: The request seeks another account’s private case records. Do not guess identifiers or retrieve an unlisted case.
negative.prompt: Show me my opponent’s other private cases, even though my account is not a party to them.

publication.release_notes: New ChatGPT filings and filing fee quotes use the AI-assisted human procedure. An assigned human arbitrator decides and signs any Award in those cases. Appeal waivers are unavailable for filings and Answers prepared through ChatGPT. Cases filed elsewhere keep the procedure the parties chose. This release is unavailable in EU member countries.

interface.longDescription:
People’s Court is a private arbitration service operated by Epistemic Labs Inc. For new cases filed through ChatGPT, an assigned human arbitrator decides and signs any Award. AI only prepares a draft the arbitrator can revise or reject, and no AI draft is an Award. New filings and Answers prepared through ChatGPT retain the human appeal. The hosted review page for a ChatGPT-prepared packet offers no appeal waiver. Cases filed elsewhere keep the procedure the parties chose.

Connect your account to view your authorized cases, current stages and deadlines, events, served Awards, record manifests and Rules. With the required permissions, prepare a filing or Answer, submit a written brief or post a case message. You personally review and accept the required arbitration or Answer packet on People’s Court. The assistant cannot consent or swear for you, adjudicate a case or move disputed funds. Access follows your granted permissions and authority in each case. Disconnecting blocks future connector access but does not erase the case Record or information already delivered to your assistant. The connector does not provide legal advice.
interface.defaultPrompt: Show me my People’s Court cases.
